featured_reviews.name: Dr Sanjay Dhawan
featured_reviews.review_text: Terrific Location. Nice lawns with almost infinity pool with children pool and excellent food and nice atmosphere to admire a clear sunset on the west coast of Mumbai. But entry is strictly for members and their guests.

featured_reviews.name: indy Ray
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lovely place to spend a Sunday chilling by the pool and enjoying their barbeque and drinks. A members only club with a long history and two pools, one sweet water and another salt water which is shaped similar in looking to the map of India.
The bbq is great, they have grilled prawns, or chicken or fish or beef to choose from! Loads of salads and other stuff as accompaniments. Unfortunately unless one knows someone who is a member, entry is next to impossible. I am just a lucky chap to know someone who signs us in and do enjoy the lazy Sunday's there. The advantage of clubs is that it's inexpensive and considering the meal costs in Bombay restaurants, it's fantastic. The other advantage of this club is that it's not as stuffy as the other ones. One can enter in shorts and flip flops, something impossible in the other member only clubs!
If you have a friend with a membership get them to take you there, it's worth a visit! Especially with its chequered past!

featured_reviews.name: Vanessa Bryan
featured_reviews.review_text:

The food was lovely and very cheap!
The service was disappointing as we had to wait 45minutes to be served after asking 3 different staff.
Overall it was great.

featured_reviews.name: Viney Mushran
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the oldest clubs in Mumbai -  devoted to swimming although they do have a few tennis courts now. An exclusive club,  open only to members. Membership entrance fees are hefty. Located in the tony, seaside residential area of Breach Candy, it has two saline pools: An indoor one and an outdoor one. The indoor one is rather shady and dark but the outdoor one is delightfully airy. Best for early evening swims in the heat and humidity of a typical Mumbai summer. There's a cozy bar-cum-cafeteria which serves meals and substantial snacks -like steak burgers - indoors in air-conditioning or in a meshed-in verandah overlooking the outdoor pool. Finish off your meal or quick bite of choice with a double espresso-on-twin-scoops of vanilla ice cream, liberally sprinkled with shaved almonds. Visiting Mumbai? Don't forget to get in touch with a member friend!

featured_reviews.review_text: A unique village in the heart of central Mumbai in Worli.Formerly a complete  fishing village having mostly a Catholic population of locals called " East Indians" but now has people from other professions and religious faiths  also living in this unique settlement in Mumbai.Some of the houses in this village are over 100. years old.

featured_reviews.name: DNYANRAJ PATKAR
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the oldest fishing village in Mumbai city which was traditional village of Koli community. Small but colourful houses and narrow lanes are main features. Now, people from all cast, creed and religion live here peacefully. The celebrations on festivals like Narali Pournima, Holi are unique here. The village also has a Fort built by Britishers to guard Mahim Bay. From top of the Fort, one can enjoy panoramic view of old village with fishing boats against the backdrop of modern highrise buildings and Worli-Bandra Sea Link.
